title: Nine Arrested After Mob Attack on BSF Personnel in Tripura's Ashabari
excerpt: Police said nine people, including three women, were arrested by Tuesday over Monday's attack that injured three BSF personnel, as a search continued for the remaining accused named in the case.
body:
• Nine people, including three women, have been arrested in connection with Monday's mob attack on BSF personnel at Ashabari in Tripura's Sepahijala district, police officials said on Tuesday — up from the eight arrests Chief Minister Manik Saha first announced.
  • Three BSF personnel, including a Company Commander, were injured in the attack and were taken for treatment; a BSF vehicle was damaged and an attempt was allegedly made to snatch a jawan's rifle.
  • Police sources in a second report said 19 people had been named in the case, and an intensive search operation launched on Monday night remained underway for the remaining accused.
  • The clash followed the apprehension of an alleged Indian smuggler near the border fence; he escaped and told villagers he had been assaulted, police officials said — a claim the investigation will need to establish.

AGARTALA — Nine people, including three women, have been arrested in connection with a mob attack on Border Security Force personnel at Ashabari in Tripura's Sepahijala district, police officials said on Tuesday, according to Nation Press. The arrests are the new development a day after the clash on Monday, in which three BSF personnel, including a Company Commander, were injured.

The count has moved since the first official announcement. Chief Minister Manik Saha, who also holds the Home portfolio, said in posts on his official X account that eight accused persons had been arrested. Police officials later put the total at nine. A second report, from Jagaran Tripura, said police sources had named 19 people in the case.

"All those involved will be brought to justice, and strict legal action will be taken against them in accordance with the law. Violence against our security personnel will not be tolerated."

— Manik Saha, Tripura Chief Minister

How Monday's clash unfolded

BSF personnel on patrol near Ashabari, under Kalamchaura police station, spotted Indian and Bangladeshi smugglers allegedly engaged in illegal cross-border trade on Monday, police officials said. The jawans apprehended one Indian smuggler, while the Bangladeshi smugglers on the other side of the border fence fled.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2117528972300800366

The detained man allegedly escaped and told local villagers that BSF personnel had assaulted him. A large mob, comprising men and women, then gathered, surrounded a BSF vehicle and attacked the personnel, leaving three injured. The injured personnel were transferred to a government hospital for treatment, Nation Press reported.

Jagaran Tripura's account adds local detail: the personnel were from the BSF's 49th Battalion, deployed at Ashabari Border Outpost, and tension escalated after a jawan allegedly struck a local resident, identified in that report as Hefzur Rahman, with a lathi. Villagers blocked the Boxanagar-Rahimpur road, and Assistant Commandant Rohit Kumar, with other personnel from Rahimpur Border Outpost, reached the spot. Those specific claims are attributed to local reports in that account and have not been established by an inquiry.

What the mob is alleged to have done

The attackers also allegedly attempted to snatch the rifle of one of the jawans and damaged a BSF vehicle, both reports said. Nation Press reported that the mob allegedly felled trees to block the road, and that one attacker was also reportedly injured during the confrontation.

Senior BSF and police officials rushed to the spot and brought the situation under control. Jagaran Tripura reported that police said the situation is now under control and normalcy has been restored in the area, and that an investigation is underway to establish the circumstances leading to the clash.

Search for the remaining accused

An intensive search operation launched on Monday night remained underway to apprehend the remaining accused, police officials said. Nation Press reported that officials did not specify the total number of suspects being sought, while Jagaran Tripura, citing police sources, put the number named in the case at 19 — which, against nine arrests, would leave others still being sought. That arithmetic relies on the 19 figure from police sources in the second report.

Leader of Opposition Jitendra Chaudhury also condemned the attack, Nation Press reported, but alleged that a section of ruling party workers is involved in illegal cross-border trade and that authorities had remained silent spectators. That is an opposition allegation, not a finding of the investigation.

A sensitive border district

Tripura shares an 856-kilometre international border with Bangladesh and is surrounded by the neighbouring country on three sides, both reports noted. Most stretches of the frontier have been fenced to prevent smuggling and illegal crossings, though enforcement remains difficult in several pockets.

For residents of the Ashabari area, the immediate questions are whether the remaining accused are arrested, what charges those arrested face in court, and what the investigation establishes about the sequence that began with the apprehension near the fence on Monday.
